content: The following are detailed professional insights into the interactions and considerations for the use of hyoscyamine with various drugs and conditions: 1. Buprenorphine (long-acting injection): Co-administration with hyoscyamine may enhance the effects of hyoscyamine due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination increases the risk of urinary retention and/or severe constipation, potentially leading to paralytic ileus. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Carbachol: Carbachol increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Cevimeline: Similar to carbachol, cevimeline increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's effect is uncertain, requiring caution and monitoring. 4. Chlorpromazine: Hyoscyamine reduces chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Conversely, chlorpromazine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is necessary. 5. Cisatracurium: Both cisatracurium and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Clomipramine: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Clozapine: Hyoscyamine decreases clozapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Clozapine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 8. Cyclizine: Both cyclizine and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Cyclobenzaprine: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Darifenacin: Both darifenacin and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. DaxibotulinumtoxinA: Hyoscyamine enhances the effects of daxibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Close monitoring is required. 12. Desipramine: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Dicyclomine: Both dicyclomine and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Dimenhydrinate: Dimenhydrinate may increase hyoscyamine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Additive anticholinergic effects may occur. Monitoring is advised. 15. Diphenhydramine: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Donepezil: Donepezil increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Donepezil may also reduce hyoscyamine's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. 17. Dosulepin: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Doxepin: Both doxepin and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Droperidol: Hyoscyamine reduces droperidol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Droperidol may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 20. Echothiophate iodide: Echothiophate iodide increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Fesoterodine: Both fesoterodine and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Flavoxate: Both flavoxate and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Fluphenazine: Hyoscyamine reduces fluphenazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Fluphenazine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 24. Galantamine: Galantamine increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Galantamine may also reduce hyoscyamine's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. 25. Glucagon: Co-administration of anticholinergic drugs and glucagon increases the risk of gastrointestinal adverse reactions due to additive effects on gastrointestinal motility inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Glycopyrrolate: Both glycopyrrolate and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Haloperidol: Hyoscyamine reduces haloperidol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Haloperidol may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 28. Henbane: Both henbane and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Homatropine: Both homatropine and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Huperzine A: Huperzine A increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Hydroxyzine: Both hydroxyzine and hyoscyamine decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Iloperidone: Hyoscyamine reduces iloperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Iloperidone may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 33. Imipramine: Both imipramine and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. IncobotulinumtoxinA: Hyoscyamine enhances the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Close monitoring is required. 35. Ipratropium: Both ipratropium and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Due to poor systemic absorption of ipratropium, interaction is unlikely at recommended dosages. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Levodopa: Anticholinergic agents may enhance the therapeutic effects of levodopa but can exacerbate tardive dyskinesia. At high doses, anticholinergics may reduce levodopa's effects by delaying gastrointestinal absorption. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Loxapine: Hyoscyamine reduces loxapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Loxapine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 38. Methscopolamine: Both methscopolamine and hyoscyamine reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Neostigmine: Neostigmine increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Olanzapine: Hyoscyamine reduces olanzapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Olanzapine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 41. Pramlintide: Co-administration with hyoscyamine is contraindicated due to synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. Avoid this combination. 42. Quetiapine: Hyoscyamine reduces quetiapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Quetiapine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 43. Risperidone: Hyoscyamine reduces risperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Risperidone may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 44. Thioridazine: Hyoscyamine reduces thioridazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Thioridazine may enhance hyoscyamine's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Close monitoring is required. 45. Pregnancy and Lactation: Hyoscyamine and methenamine are excreted in human milk, so caution is advised in breastfeeding women. For pregnancy, hyoscyamine is categorized as Category C, indicating that risk cannot be ruled out. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk.
